notes: Military frontiers advance by adjacent ranks; large leaps are strongly blocked.
Food systems spread well when settlement patterns can absorb them.
Materials require craft infrastructure and resource familiarity.
Energy systems are infrastructure-heavy and slower to diffuse.
Transport ideas spread along routes but depend on terrain and materials.
Maritime skills spread best through port networks and navigable routes.
Writing and communication can become cultural currency quickly.
Administrative innovations benefit strongly from shared polity institutions.
Medical knowledge spreads unevenly and needs trusted practitioners.
Formal knowledge needs specialists and often follows institutions.
Craft processes spread through apprenticeships and trade.
Cultural forms spread readily but give modest direct prosperity.
Computing requires a deep supporting technical base.
Household and everyday practices diffuse broadly once useful.
